newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil handed 3.2 bln-real check for CVRD - reports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil handed 3.2 bln-real check for CVRD - reports.

text.p: Brazil's government was handed a check for nearly 3.2 billion reais ($3.0 bln) as payment for a controlling stake in Cia Vale do Rio Doce sold in a privatization auction Tuesday, local newspapers said Saturday.

The mining giant officially became a private company Friday when the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange, which held the auction, turned over the check to the federal National Development Bank (BNDES), papers said.
Marking the close of Latin America's largest privatization ever, leading Brazilian papers on Saturday displayed photographs of the 3,199,974,496-real Banco Bradesco check on their front pages.
A group led by Brazilian steelmaker Cia Siderurgica Nacional and including U.S.-based NationsBank won bidding on the 41.73-percent voting stake in CVRD with an offer of 3.34 billion reais.
Folha de S. Paulo daily said the Rio bolsa deposited the remaining 138.2 million reais ($130 million) in the accounts of investors who sold their CVRD shares in conjunction with the privatization.
The government's 3.2 billion-real share would be split between the BNDES and the National Treasury, which will use its nearly 1.6 billion-real stake to reduce government debt, papers said.
The BNDES plans to use its roughly 1.6 billion-real portion to finance infrastructure projects, they said.

Along with the check, Joao Fraga, head of the Rio bolsa's Liquidation and Custody Chamber, also handed the BNDES a "golden share" that gives the government the right to veto the sale of CVRD assets over the next five years, they added.
The government continues to hold 36 percent of CVRD's common, or voting shares, but will sell a 4.4-percent voting stake to workers in coming days, Folha said.
It also expects to garner another 2.0 billion reais late this year when it sells its remaining CVRD common, totalling a 31.6 percent voting stake, it added.
